sentences.text:
For ready reference, the same is reproduced hereinunder:-
"1.

Heard Mr. Jitendra Singh Patel Advocate holding brief of Mr. Neeraj Srivastava,
the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State and Mrs. Vijeta Kushwaha, the learned counsel representing first informant.
2. Perused the record.

3. Instant bail application has been filed by applicant-Govind seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.132 of 2022 under Sections 376 (2) N, 323,
506 I.P.C. Police Station-Partapur, District-Meerut, during the pendency of trial.

4. Record shows that in respect of an incident, which is alleged to have occurred on 28.08.2021 a delayed F.I.R. dated 16.04.2022 was lodged by first informant Arun (brother of the prosecutrix) and was registered as Case Crime No.132 of 2022 under Sections 376 (2) N, 323, 506 I.P.C. Police Station-Partapur, District-Meerut.
In the aforesaid F.I.R. two persons namely Gopal and Govind (applicant herein) have been nominated as named accused.
5. The gravamen of the allegations made in the F.I.R is to the effect that named accused are guilty of dislodging the modesty of the prosecutrix deliberately and forcibly by committing rape upon her.

6. It is apposite to mention here that applicant Govind is the brother-in-law of the deceased (husband of the sister of first informant).
7.
After aforementioned F.I.R. was registered, Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of above-mentioned case crime number in terms of Chapter XII Cr.P.C.
During course of investigation substantial material was collected.
On the basis of above and other material collected by him during course of investigation, he came to the conclusion that complicity of named accused is clearly established against named accused.
He accordingly submitted the charge-sheet dated 08.07.2022 whereby accused Gopal has been charge-sheeted under Sections 376 (2) N, 323, 506 I.P.C.

Thereafter, Investigating Officer submitted a supplementary charge sheet dated 06.10.2022 against applicant whereby applicant Govind has been charge-sheeted under Sections 376 (2) N, 323, 506 I.P.C.
8.

Present application for bail came up for consideration on 07.08.2023 and this Court passed the following order:
" Heard Mr. Neeraj Srivastava, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A.
for state, Mr. Mahendra Kumar yadav and Vijeta Kushwaha, the learned counsel for Govind vs State Of U.P.

on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110967847/
2
first informant.
An affidavit of compliance has been filed by learned A.G.A. in Court today, which is taken on record.

With reference to the affidavit of compliance,
learned A.G.A. submits that sample for DNA test of Gopal was not initially taken but was taken subsequently.
He, therefore contends that hearing of present application for bail be adjourned.
In view of above, hearing of present application is adjourned.
Matter shall re-appear as fresh on 6.9.2023.

Order Date :- 7.8.2023 "
9.
Subsequent to above order dated 07.08.2023, DNA profile of applicant, the mother and new born child was conducted.
As per DNA report, applicant and mother i.e. prosecutrix are reported to be the biological parents of the new born child.

10. Learned counsel for applicant contends that though the applicant is a named as well as charge-sheeted accused inasmuch as charge sheet has been submitted against applicant on 06.10.2022 yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.
Applicant is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
Allegations made in the F.I.R. are false and concocted.
Present criminal proceedings have been engineered on account of an ulterior motive.
Considering the relationship of the parties, applicant cannot be said to have committed the crime in question.
11. Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in custody since 05.10.2022.
As such, he has undergone more than eleven and a half months of incarceration.

Police report (charge-sheet) in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted, therefore, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallised.
However, upto this stage, no such incriminating circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
On the above premise, he submits that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
12. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. for State and the learned counsel representing first informant have vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
They submit that since applicant is a named and charged sheeted accused therefore he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.

They further submit that complicity of applicant in the crime in question is fully established as per the DNA report of the new born child, Copy of the same has been brought on record as Annexure 1 to the compliance affidavit filed by the learned A.G.A.
The prosecutrix is sister in law i.e. sali of the applicant.
Applicant is guilty of dislodging the modesty of sister-in-law of the prosecutrix.

The prosecutrix in her statement under Section 161/164 Cr.P.C. has supported the F.I.R. Upto this stage,
there is nothing on record to infer malicious or false prosecution of the applicant.
As such no sympathy be shown by this Court in favour of applicant.
No good or sufficient ground exists to enlarge the applicant on bail.
13. When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.

Govind vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110967847/
3 14.

Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, the learned counsel representing first informant, upon consideration of material on record, evidence, gravity and nature of offence, accusations made as well as complicity of applicant coupled with the fact that medical report and DNA report clearly establish the complicity of applicant in the crime in question, the prosecutrix in her statements under Sections 161/164 Cr.P.C. has fully supported the F.I.R. there is nothing on record to infer consent of the prosecutrix, applicant is guilty of dislodging the modesty of the prosecutrix, who is his sister-in-law, applicant has caused breach of trust and relationship between the parties, therefore irrespective of the submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant in support of this application for bail, this Court does not find any sufficient or good ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
15. As a result, present application for bail fails and is liable to be rejected.
16. It is accordingly rejected."
5. Learned counsel for applicant contends that subsequent to the order dated 27.09.2023, the trial of the applicant commenced before court below.
The prosecutrix has deposed before court below as PW2 whereas, the first informant has deposed before court below as PW1.
However, both the witnesses have not supported the F.I.R.

On the above conspectus, he thus submits that once the statements of the first informant and the prosecutrix have been recorded then no good ground exists to prolong the custodial arrest of applicant.
In case, applicant is enlarged on bail, then it cannot be said that the applicant shall either terrorize the witnesses or shall hamper the course of trial.

He,
therefore, contends that once the prosecutrix has herself not supported the F.I.R. no good ground exists to continue the custodial arrest of applicant.
6. Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as, he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in jail since 05.10.2023.
As such, he has undergone more than 3 months of incarceration.
The police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted.
As such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallized.
However, up to this stage, no such circumstance has emerged on record necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
On the above premise, it is thus urged that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
7. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.
Attention of the court was invited to the order dated 27.09.2023 passed by this Court on the first bail of applicant.
With reference to above, the learned A.G.A. submits that as per the D.N.A. report, applicant is the biological father of the new born child.

On the above premise, the learned A.G.A. contends that in view of aforementioned conclusive piece of evidence criminality committed by the applicant is fully established inasmuch as no marriage was solemnized in between the applicant and the prosecutrix.
He, therefore, contends that applicant does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.

However, he could not dislodge the factual and legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant in support of the present repeat application for bail with reference to the record at this stage.

Govind vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110967847/
4
8. When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.

9. Having heard, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence, complicity of accused, accusation made coupled with the fact that as per the D.N.A. report, applicant is the biological father of the new born child,
therefore, irrespective of the fact the prosecutrix and the first informant in their deposition before court below have not supported the F.I.R, therefore, irrespective of the varied submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant in support of the present repeat application for bail by the learned counsel for applicant, this Court does not find any new or good ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
10. As a result, the present repeat application for bail fails and is liable to be rejected.
11. It is, accordingly, rejected.
